last_attempts_log.asr_text: My young child picked videos that were too much for them, and things in the app that could cost money, just because they were interested. When I talk to them, they often say, Then I won't do it. I think they understand when I explain it, but maybe they can't see what's wrong before they choose. I don't think it's okay to let them use anything they happen to like. Seeing this, I feel safer if there are rules for using social media at different ages. But honestly, on a long trip, I want them to be quiet. It helps if they watch something. Limits are hard on parents, too. Even so, I still can't say how far I want the rules to go.

last_attempts_log.asr_text: I don't want people to stop me using social media just because of my age. If even high school students couldn't have accounts, it would be hard to keep in touch with friends. I'm against the ban. I want a say in what I can use and how I use it. I want to decide for myself, but I can't handle everything that happens on my own. If people say bad things about me or threaten me, I'd still want to go to an adult right away. Maybe that's selfish of me. Instead of giving everyone the same limits because of their age, I think we can do other things, like set safety filters. I want the way we deal with this to fit how we use it, but we should still be able to keep in touch with friends.

last_attempts_log.asr_text: As a parent of a middle school child, I want to choose how much they use social media, based on what they can handle. Rather than draw a line based only on age, I think it would be better, if possible, to let them use more features step-by-step, as they learn to handle them. I don't want the only choices to be letting them use it or banning it. I want different steps. If my child started using social media with no preparation as soon as they reached the age when it had been banned, I would worry. I don't think reaching the age when it's okay to use it means they'll suddenly know how to keep themselves safe. Just as you need to practice swimming before going into the sea, it's still scary when a child who isn't ready is suddenly thrown into it.
